cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: damaged – harmed or spoiled; not in perfect condition.

p.em: Example: The old guitar was damaged during the long journey.

cosy-blockquote.p: normal – conforming to a standard; usual, typical, or expected.

p.em: Example: It is completely normal to feel nervous before a big presentation.

cosy-blockquote.p: special – better, greater, or otherwise different from what is usual.

p.em: Example: She prepared a special dinner to celebrate her promotion.

cosy-blockquote.p: different – not the same as another or each other; unlike in nature.

p.em: Example: They have completely different opinions about the new movie.

cosy-blockquote.p: movies – motion pictures or films shown in a theater.

p.em: Example: They love to watch bad movies on a rainy Sunday afternoon.

cosy-blockquote.p: summer – The warmest season of the year, often associated with youth and freedom.

p.em: Example: They promised to stay best friends forever during that unforgettable summer break.

cosy-blockquote.p: dancing – the activity of moving the body to music.

p.em: Example: Dancing is a beautiful way to express your emotions and joy.

cosy-blockquote.p: tonight – on the present or coming night.

p.em: Example: We are going to attend a live music concert tonight.

cosy-blockquote.p: choose – pick out or select someone or something as being the best.

p.em: Example: You must choose a career path that truly inspires you.

cosy-blockquote.p: right – morally good, justified, or acceptable; correct.

p.em: Example: She did the right thing by telling the truth to her friend.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Share whether you agree or disagree with these statements and discuss them with your teacher:

ul.li: Incorrect: There is a big improvement of → Correct: There is a big improvement in my English ((Use 'in' after 'improvement' to express domain.))
Incorrect: It was a great relief of → Correct: It was a great relief to hear the news ((Use 'relief' + infinitive 'to hear'.))
Incorrect: She is in the choir since → Correct: She has been in the choir for three years ((Use present perfect + 'for' to show duration of state.))
